candidate.claim: Honda–Tate packages a finite-field abelian variety through its Frobenius Weil number, endomorphism algebra, isogeny class, and field of definition. The Taniyama extension raises the same reciprocity pattern to a group-level object governing CM motivic Galois actions and conjugation of Shimura data, replacing many objectwise actions by one symmetry group and cocycle.
candidate.historical_or_program_relation: This is a change of scale within the geometry of L-functions: explicit Frobenius classification supplies object-level arithmetic data, while the Taniyama group seeks the shared reciprocity mechanism across CM motives and Shimura varieties.
candidate.limits: The two constructions operate in different settings, and forgetting the base field can already collapse distinct Honda–Tate situations. Identifying the common extension does not prove the conjugation conjecture, supply RH, or classify non-CM motives.
candidate.title: CM reciprocity scales from individual Frobenius classes to a common motivic symmetry extension
